news_drafts.headline: Colchester reorganisation panel hears of reported £13.2m adult social care overspend at Essex County Council
news_drafts.lead:
A member of Colchester's Local Government Reorganisation (LGR) Transformation and Transition Panel referred to "a reported £13.2 million overspend in adult social care at Essex County Council", according to the panel's draft minutes of 9 September 2026.

The figure came up in discussion of the underlying financial and service pressures facing the area. The minutes describe it as a reported figure for another authority. They do not say how it was sourced, or which year or part of a year it covers.

The £13.2m is Essex County Council's figure, not Colchester's, and the minutes are still in draft.
news_drafts.paper_title: LGR Transformation and Transition Panel draft minutes - 9 September 2026

news_drafts.headline: Colchester's forecast 2026-27 day-to-day deficit falls from £2.4m at quarter 1 to about £1m at quarter 2
news_drafts.lead:
Colchester City Council's General Fund, the account that pays for council services other than housing and schools, is forecast to overspend by about £1 million this year, down from £2.4m forecast at the end of the first quarter. Officers gave the quarter 2 figure as an "emerging" position to the Governance and Audit Committee, whose draft minutes of 8 September 2026 record it.

The quarter 1 forecast was driven by temporary accommodation and homelessness, waste, and the corporate landlord function. Officers told the committee the forecast is a point-in-time assessment and that the position has improved since quarter 1. They also said the quarter 2 figure could prove optimistic. A similar deficit at the same stage of the previous year ended with a small surplus.

The minutes also record a forecast shortfall at Leisure World, which covers the pool, personal training, beauty services and Aqua Springs. The shortfall arose from Leisure World income targets, and investment in the pool is intended to improve future income. Officers said a sinking fund, a pot of money built up over time for a known future cost, might be needed to manage risks including vacant units at the Northern Gateway Leisure Park.
news_drafts.paper_title: Governance and Audit Committee draft minutes - 8 September 2026

news_drafts.headline: Colchester panel cites reported £13.2m adult social care overspend at Essex County Council
news_drafts.lead:
A member of Colchester's Local Government Reorganisation (LGR) Transformation and Transition Panel pointed to a reported £13.2 million overspend in adult social care at Essex County Council, the papers for the Cabinet meeting of 21 October 2026 show. Adult social care is the council service that provides care and support for adults.

The reference appears in the panel's recommendation to Cabinet at item 08(iv). The papers say the panel member highlighted "underlying financial and service pressures in the wider Essex area" and gave the figure as context for continued partnership working.

The overspend is Essex County Council's, not Colchester's. The papers give no period for it and no breakdown of where within adult social care it arose. They do not say what Cabinet is asked to decide in response to it.

findings.detail: The figure was raised during discussion of the underlying financial and service pressures facing the area. It is a reported figure for another authority, and the paper does not say how it was sourced.

findings.paper_title: LGR Transformation and Transition Panel draft minutes - 9 September 2026
findings.headline: Colchester is recording its LGR expenditure and resources so it can seek reimbursement from Government, with overall LGR activity to be reduced
findings.detail: The Chair said the Council would review its LGR commitments, taking account of contractual obligations and employment responsibilities, and that overall activity would be reduced. A Panel member said the Council would quantify the costs already incurred. The paper gives no £ figure for those costs.
findings.matters: Abortive preparatory spend on a paused reorganisation is a cost a finance director may need to quantify, reclaim, or write off, and the paper gives no total for it.
findings.quote: Expenditure and resource allocation were being recorded and would be reported to the Panel, supporting any future request to Government for reimbursement.

findings.paper_title: Item 7(i) - Colchester Borough Homes Annual Governance Statement 2025-26
findings.headline: The Head of Internal Audit's opinion is expressly not an opinion on CBH's ongoing financial viability or its ability to meet financial obligations.
findings.detail: TIAA's opinion is that CBH has reasonable and effective risk management, control and governance processes for the areas reviewed. The opinion is limited to matters found in the reviews carried out during the year, and the paper says viability must be assured from other sources.
findings.matters: A lender or finance director reading an ALMO's assurance package will want to know which parts of its financial health the internal audit opinion covers, and this paper states that viability is not one of them.
findings.quote: ongoing financial viability or your ability to meet financial obligations

findings.paper_title: Item 7(i) - Colchester Borough Homes Annual Governance Statement 2025-26
findings.headline: The council's 2025/26 management fee to CBH totals £14,716,928, of which £11,828,880 is HRA revenue.
findings.detail: The fee is broken down into HRA revenue (base fee, repairs overheads and repairs works), HRA capital, and General Fund revenue for housing options and homelessness work. The paper says the principal items in the financial statements but not in the fee relate to subcontracted repairs, voids and compliance work.
findings.matters: The management fee is the council's own cash flowing into the ALMO, so its split across HRA and General Fund is the figure a council finance director needs to track against the housing budget.

findings.paper_title: Item 7(i) - Colchester Borough Homes Annual Governance Statement 2025-26
findings.headline: CBH reports a 2025/26 surplus of £121,345 on total revenue of £25,061,050 against total expenditure of £24,939,705.
findings.detail: The surplus is the difference between total revenue and total expenditure in the summary of CBH's 2025/26 financial statements. Employee costs were £10,234,207 and service delivery direct costs were £11,744,079, of which sub-contractor costs were £11,046,945.
findings.matters: A small surplus on a company whose income is largely the council's own management fee shows how little margin sits between what the council pays and what the company spends.
